title: UNIT 7: CONGRUENCY AND SIMILARITY
notes:
✓ Congruency → Two figures have exactly the same shape and size.

✓ Similarity → Two figures have the same shape, but their sizes may be different.

title: 7.1 CONGRUENT TRIANGLES
notes:
✓ Congruent triangles → Triangles with corresponding sides equal in length and corresponding angles equal in measure.

◆ Symbol:
△ABC ≅ △DEF

✓ Therefore:
AB = DE, BC = EF, AC = DF
∠A = ∠D, ∠B = ∠E, ∠C = ∠F

title: CONGRUENCY CRITERIA
notes:
◆ SSS → Three corresponding sides are equal.

◆ SAS → Two corresponding sides and the included angle are equal.

◆ ASA → Two corresponding angles and the included side are equal.

◆ RHS → For right triangles, equal hypotenuse and one corresponding side are sufficient.

title: CONGRUENCY VS SIMILARITY
notes:
✓ Congruent → Same shape AND same size.

✓ Similar → Same shape, but size may differ.

✓ Congruent figures have scale factor 1.

✓ Congruent figures are always similar, but similar figures are not necessarily congruent.

title: 7.2 SIMILAR FIGURES
notes:
✓ Two plane figures are similar when:

Corresponding angles are congruent.
Corresponding sides are proportional.

◆ Symbol:
△ABC ~ △DEF

This means:
∠A = ∠D, ∠B = ∠E, ∠C = ∠F

✓ AB/DE = BC/EF = AC/DF

title: SCALE FACTOR
notes:
✓ Scale factor → Ratio of corresponding sides of similar figures.

✓ Scale factor = Corresponding side of enlargement ÷ Corresponding side of original

◆ k > 1 → Enlargement
◆ 0 < k < 1 → Reduction
◆ k = 1 → Same size

title: CORRESPONDING SIDES & ANGLES
notes:
For:
△ABC ~ △DEF

✓ Corresponding vertices:
A ↔ D, B ↔ E, C ↔ F

✓ Corresponding sides:
AB ↔ DE
BC ↔ EF
AC ↔ DF

✓ Corresponding angles:
∠A ↔ ∠D
∠B ↔ ∠E
∠C ↔ ∠F

title: 7.3 AA SIMILARITY
notes:
✓ AA Similarity Theorem → If two angles of one triangle are equal to two corresponding angles of another triangle, the triangles are similar.

✓ Only two angles are needed because the third angles are automatically equal since the angles of a triangle sum to 180°.

title: SSS SIMILARITY
notes:
✓ SSS Similarity Theorem → If all three pairs of corresponding sides of two triangles are proportional, the triangles are similar.

✓ AB/DE = BC/EF = AC/DF

✓ All three ratios must be equal.

title: SAS SIMILARITY
notes:
✓ SAS Similarity Theorem → If two pairs of corresponding sides are proportional and the included angles are equal, the triangles are similar.

✓ The equal angle must be the INCLUDED angle between the two proportional sides.

title: PROPORTIONALITY IN SIMILAR TRIANGLES
notes:
If:
△ABC ~ △DEF

✓ Then:
AB/DE = BC/EF = AC/DF = k

✓ Use these equal ratios to find unknown side lengths.

✓ Match corresponding sides carefully before forming the proportion.

title: 7.4 RATIO OF PERIMETERS
notes:
✓ For similar plane figures:

Ratio of perimeters = Ratio of corresponding sides.

✓ P₁/P₂ = s₁/s₂

✓ If the scale factor is k:
P₁/P₂ = k

✓ Doubling all lengths doubles the perimeter; tripling all lengths triples the perimeter.

title: 7.5 RATIO OF AREAS
notes:
✓ For similar plane figures:

Ratio of areas = Square of the ratio of corresponding sides.

✓ A₁/A₂ = (s₁/s₂)²

✓ If the scale factor is k:
A₁/A₂ = k²

✓ Doubling lengths → area becomes 4 times.
✓ Tripling lengths → area becomes 9 times.

title: CIRCLES & SIMILARITY
notes:
✓ All circles are similar.

✓ Scale factor of circles = Ratio of their corresponding radii.

✓ Circumference ratio = Ratio of radii.

✓ Area ratio = Square of the ratio of radii.

title: SCALE FACTOR IN CONSTRUCTION
notes:
◆ k > 1 → Constructed figure is larger.

◆ 0 < k < 1 → Constructed figure is smaller.

◆ k = 1 → Constructed figure has the same size.

Example:
Scale factor = 5/3 → enlargement.
Scale factor = 1/2 → reduction.

title: HEIGHT USING SHADOWS
notes:
✓ When an object and a person form similar triangles using their shadows:

Object height / Object shadow = Person height / Person shadow

✓ Therefore:
Object height = (Object shadow × Person height) ÷ Person shadow

✓ Always compare corresponding heights and shadows.

title: PYTHAGORAS FROM SIMILAR TRIANGLES
notes:
✓ Similarity can be used to prove the Pythagorean theorem.

✓ For a right triangle with legs a and b and hypotenuse c:

a² + b² = c²

✓ If the perpendicular from the right angle to the hypotenuse has length p:

pc = ab

1/p² = 1/a² + 1/b²

title: QUICK REVISION FORMULAS
notes:
◆ Similar triangles:
✓ AB/DE = BC/EF = AC/DF = k

◆ Scale factor:
✓ k = Corresponding new side ÷ Corresponding original side

◆ Perimeter ratio:
✓ P₁/P₂ = k

◆ Area ratio:
✓ A₁/A₂ = k²

◆ Shadow problems:
✓ Height₁/Shadow₁ = Height₂/Shadow₂

◆ Pythagorean theorem:
✓ a² + b² = c²

◆ Similarity criteria:
✓ AA • SSS • SAS

◆ Congruency criteria:
✓ SSS • SAS • ASA • RHS
